reason: The passage demonstrates God's active support and care for the Hebrew people through multiple explicit actions: (1) God responds to their prayer ('שְׁמַ֤ע אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙' - 'Hear our God'); (2) God thwarts the enemies' plans ('וַיָּ֥פֶר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־ עֲצָתָ֑ם' - 'God thwarted their counsel'); (3) God explicitly promises to fight for the people ('אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יִלָּ֥חֶם לָֽנוּ' - 'Our God will fight for us'); and (4) the people successfully complete their work with divine protection. These narrative elements collectively demonstrate divine support for the Hebrew people's welfare and success, which is consistent with the statement that Yahweh wants them to be well.
